subsystems.name: Plasma source
subsystems.role: ionizes neutral gas into a hot, electrically conductive plasma.

subsystems.name: Ion heating stage
subsystems.role: adds energy to the plasma using radio waves tuned to ion motion.

subsystems.name: Magnetic nozzle
subsystems.role: converts the plasma's thermal energy into a directed exhaust jet.

subsystems.name: Superconducting magnet system
subsystems.role: confines and shapes the plasma without physical walls.

subsystems.name: Power and propellant feed
subsystems.role: supplies the hundreds of kilowatts of electricity and the gas the thruster consumes.
parts: high-power solar arrays or nuclear reactor

buildSteps.title: Design the magnetic field
buildSteps.detail: Computer models shape the field so plasma stays off the walls and exhausts in one direction.

buildSteps.title: Wind the superconducting coils
buildSteps.detail: Niobium-titanium or high-temperature superconductor wire is wound into coils that must survive launch vibrations.

buildSteps.title: Build the helicon source
buildSteps.detail: A quartz tube is wrapped with an antenna and connected to a radio-frequency power supply.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the heating section
buildSteps.detail: A second antenna and magnetic mirror are added downstream to boost ion energy.

buildSteps.title: Fit the magnetic nozzle
buildSteps.detail: A set of coils creates a diverging field that lets the plasma expand and accelerate.

buildSteps.title: Integrate cryogenics and power
buildSteps.detail: Cryocoolers, power conditioning and propellant plumbing are attached and insulated.

buildSteps.title: Vacuum-chamber test
buildSteps.detail: The thruster is fired in a large vacuum tank to measure thrust, efficiency and thermal loads.

buildSteps.title: Space-qualify and launch
buildSteps.detail: The unit is ruggedised for launch, then operated on a test satellite or orbital tug.

prerequisites.why: a VASIMR needs hundreds of kilowatts to megawatts; solar arrays become impractically large beyond a few hundred kilowatts.
ground prototypes exist, but they need cryocoolers and radiation shielding that add mass.
laboratory tests have run for minutes; a cargo mission would need weeks or months of continuous firing.
vacuum-tube and solid-state amplifiers at the required frequencies are commercially available.
inert gases are already used in ion thrusters and can be stored at high pressure.

pathway.milestone: laboratory thrusters running at ~200 kW for minutes
pathway.unlocks: data on thrust, efficiency and plasma behaviour.

pathway.milestone: in-space demonstration on a small satellite or the ISS
pathway.unlocks: proof that the thruster works in vacuum and microgravity for extended periods.
moving heavy cargo between low Earth orbit and the Moon or geostationary orbit.
fast, frequent cargo and crew missions to Mars and beyond.
